text_summary: WHO 7-sign IMCI algorithm recommended to identify infants aged 0-59 days with possible SBI needing further evaluation/treatment (non-hospital settings)
Infants aged 0-59 days with IMCI signs of critical illness should be referred to hospital
If referral for critical illness not possible: ampicillin IM/IV plus gentamicin IM/IV for at least 10 days
Clinical severe infection, referral not possible (regimen 4): oral amoxicillin for at least 7 days plus gentamicin IM/IV for at least 7 days
Clinical severe infection, if 7 days of gentamicin IM not feasible (regimen 3): oral amoxicillin for at least 7 days plus gentamicin IM/IV for only 2 days
Fast breathing as only sign, aged 0-6 days, referral not possible: oral amoxicillin for at least 7 days
Fast breathing as only sign, aged 7-59 days: oral amoxicillin for at least 7 days, can be managed outside hospital
No recommendation on hospital-based clinical-sign algorithms for diagnosing sepsis (0-59 days); labs used in reviewed studies not feasible in low-resource settings
Hospitalized, suspected sepsis (0-59 days): ampicillin IM/IV plus gentamicin IM/IV for at least 10 days, first-choice
Hospitalized, suspected staphylococcal sepsis (0-59 days): cloxacillin IM/IV plus gentamicin IM/IV for at least 10 days, first-choice (pathogen-directed)

Hospitalized, suspected meningitis (0-59 days): ampicillin, cefotaxime or ceftriaxone IM/IV plus gentamicin IM/IV for at least 3 weeks, first-choice; add ampicillin to third-gen cephalosporin+gentamicin (triple therapy) if Listeria monocytogenes suspected
Hospitalized, suspected pneumonia (0-59 days): ampicillin IM/IV plus gentamicin IM/IV for at least 7 days, first-choice
Hospitalized, suspected staphylococcal pneumonia (0-59 days): cloxacillin IM/IV plus gentamicin IM/IV for at least 7 days, first-choice (pathogen-directed)
